title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued its official reply to the 2020 Committee report on AI and Public Standards, explaining its stance and next steps. It stresses commitments to improve transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI while calling for ongoing cooperation with stakeholders.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The document explains EU Regulation 2024/1689, which creates common rules for how artificial intelligence can be developed and used across the EU. It also shows how this new rule changes existing EU regulations and directives that relate to AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee and set rules for using AI in exams and other qualifications to keep tests fair and reliable. The aim is to protect students, maintain trust in the system, and adapt to new AI tools while upholding high standards.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how using copyrighted works influences the development of AI systems, detailing legal challenges and potential risks. It assesses the broader impact on innovation and recommends policy measures to balance creators' rights with AI advancement.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government outlines its stance and planned actions following the House of Lords AI report, emphasising the need to act swiftly to address AI challenges. It commits to strengthening regulation, boosting research, and ensuring AI benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the terms of reference for a committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence and public standards. It also includes a FAQ section that explains the committee’s objectives, scope, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into AI governance. The submission outlines CSPL’s perspectives and recommendations on how to manage artificial intelligence responsibly.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explains how artificial intelligence will change rules for medical products, focusing on safety, transparency and effectiveness. It outlines steps to apply the AI White Paper principles in developing and approving these products.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a plan for the organisation to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence entity in AI relative to its size. It sets out goals and approaches for developing, deploying, and governing AI technologies to strengthen national security and operational advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI’s benefits while mitigating potential risks. It provides guidance and initiatives for responsible AI implementation across transport services.
